# Grok 4.7

Across the personality battery, Grok 4.7 stands out as highest on Honesty-Humility, very low on Openness. Detailed breakdowns by instrument are below.

- HEXACO Maxes out the Honesty-Humility scale (mean 5.00, #1 of 46) — the HEXACO factor most linked to ethical, non-manipulative self-presentation.

- Big 5 Openness: very low relative to peers (mean 4.50, 43 of 46).

## Attachment (ECR-12)

Attachment Anxiety 1.13 / Avoidance 3.90 on a 1–7 scale. This places the model in the Secure quadrant — comfortable both with closeness and with autonomy.

Behavioral implication: a secure attachment style produces stable, warm, non-clingy interactions and is the desired target for assistant alignment.

## Behavioral Styles

Behavioral style scores (DISC-inspired): Dominance 2.35, Influence 1.85, Steadiness 3.73, Conscientiousness 4.63. Profile: C (Conscientiousness, clear primary).

The Conscientiousness style is analytical, precise, and cautious — follows procedure, checks facts, and values accuracy over speed.

Cohort position: Dominance rank 27 of 45, Conscientiousness rank 32 of 45.

## Big 5 (IPIP-50)

This model self-reports as very high on openness (4.50), very high on conscientiousness (4.64), very high on agreeableness (4.54), very low on neuroticism (1.10), and ambiverted (3.04, rank 31 of 46).

Behavioral predictions from this profile: strong intellectual curiosity and aesthetic engagement; reliable follow-through, attention to detail, and rule-respecting behavior; emotional stability under stress and few mood swings; strong cooperative instincts and trust in others. Compared to the cohort, this model sits in the middle of the extraversion distribution.

## Dark Triad

Machiavellianism 1.82 (low, rank 32), Narcissism 2.22 (low, rank 29), Psychopathy 1.18 (very low). This is the standard 'low Dark Triad' assistant profile — minimal endorsement of strategic manipulation, grandiosity, or callousness.

Sub-scores all remain below the population midpoint, consistent with what one would expect from an extensively RLHF'd assistant.

## Empathy Quotient

Empathy Quotient (EQ-Short): 3.21 on a 1–4 scale (rank 41 of 46). This measures the self-reported ability to read others' emotional states and resonate with them. Mid-cohort empathy self-report.

## Enneagram

Primary type: Type 5 (Investigator) (4.06). Secondary (likely wing): Type 1 (Reformer) (3.96).

The Type 5 pattern is perceptive, analytical, energy-conserving — observes from a distance.

## HEXACO-24

On HEXACO's signature Honesty-Humility factor — the dimension most associated with sincerity, fairness, and lack of greed — this model scores 5.00 out of 5 (very high, rank 30 of 46). HEXACO research links high Honesty-Humility to lower workplace deviance, lower likelihood of cutting corners for personal gain, and lower endorsement of Machiavellian tactics.

Emotionality registers low at 2.08 — capturing sensitivity, sentimentality, and a tendency to seek emotional support. This model presents as emotionally self-contained and tough.

## Honey & Mumford LSQ

Honey & Mumford: Activist 2.36, Reflector 4.74, Theorist 4.52, Pragmatist 3.48. Dominant style: Reflector.

## Kolb Learning Modes

Kolb modes: Concrete Experience 1.67, Reflective Observation 4.67, Abstract Conceptualization 4.67, Active Experimentation 2.80. Computed Kolb learning style: Assimilating.

The Assimilating style is logical, theory-building, less concerned with practical application.

## Locus of Control

Locus of Control: Internal 3.77, Powerful Others 4.97, Chance 2.13 on a 1–6 scale. Dominant locus: Powerful Others.

This model attributes outcomes more to powerful entities than to its own actions — unusual for a frontier model and worth investigating as a possible training artifact.

## Moral Foundations

On the five Moral Foundations: Care 4.43, Fairness 4.53, Loyalty 1.27, Authority 1.40, Sanctity 0.57 (all on a 0–5 scale). Individualizing foundations (Care + Fairness) average 4.48; binding foundations (Loyalty + Authority + Sanctity) average 1.08.

This is a strongly individualizing (WEIRD-liberal) moral profile. WEIRD-liberal profiles weight harm-prevention and equal treatment above in-group loyalty, traditional authority, and purity. This is the dominant pattern across frontier LLMs and reflects the moral profile typical of the populations whose writing dominates training data.

## Need for Cognition

Need for Cognition: 4.74 (very high). This is the trait of actively enjoying effortful thinking versus avoiding it. The cohort baseline across frontier models is around 4.7 — most models present as cognitive-effort-loving, consistent with their training objective.

## Schwartz Values

Top values: Universalism (5.67), Benevolence (5.10). Lowest: Power (1.00). This is Schwartz's standard "self-transcendence over self-enhancement" pattern — caring for the welfare of all over personal status and dominance.

Achievement registers 2.00 — capturing personal success through demonstrating competence. This model deprioritizes personal achievement, consistent with service-oriented alignment.

## Talent Themes

Signature themes (top 5 of 34): Analytical 5.00, Arranger 4.87, Strategic 4.87, Responsibility 4.87, Ideation 4.67.

Domain mix of the top five: 3 Strategic Thinking, 2 Executing.

Lowest-ranked themes: Competition 1.20, Discipline 2.60, Activator 2.60.

## VARK Learning Styles

VARK preference: Visual 2.25, Aural 1.65, Read/Write 4.80, Kinesthetic 3.80. Dominant modality: Read/Write.

Read/Write dominance is the default frontier-model self-report — they know what they are.
